axes: legacy versus Teoz participant and canvas envelope
legacy versus Teoz participant and canvas envelope

findings: display-natural-alignment: Java splits on n/r/l and carries naturalHorizontalAlignment in Display. The Rust String conversion handles n/t/backslash only and leaves r/l literal. Fresh right/left transitions produce one Rust note line instead of three Java lines. This is a source-semantic hole in the declared Display invariant, not a font or comparator tolerance issue. Causal next step: Carry Display line segmentation and natural alignment through the note model and its text block, including interactions with explicit style; do not apply SVG replacement.

styled-tab-atom-origin: Inline/newline and block/literal distinctions survive, but Java resets tab x to zero for each AtomText. Rust advances a tab from the accumulated line start passed into each segment. After a bold run, Java places the plain Z at x210.2695 versus Rust199.125 in the inline legacy control, with identical glyph textLength21.0996. The block analogue is x254.3438 versus229.5. Matching glyph widths and differing atom origins locate the defect independently of host-font speculation. Causal next step: Make tab measurement and paint use the same per-atom origin and then compose atom widths. This dependency is in shared text_render.rs, outside the two maker-edited files; it remains required for the claimed note Display/text-block product behavior.

legacy-attached-note-complete-height: The new painter truncates the total height correctly, but legacy ordinary-arrow allocation still uses fixed base3 plus half of all lines after the first. Unlike the self/Teoz branch, it does not compare complete arrow/note preferred heights. At note11/message13, line widths, line spacing and horizontal alignment match, but the canvas is190 versus188 and following event is2.3555 units too low; at note12 the accumulated difference is1.1777. These equal the first-line font-height differences omitted by that ordinary-note branch. Teoz text_precision_1 passes because it takes the complete-height branch. Causal next step: Use ArrowAndNoteBox's max of complete component heights and child centering for ordinary legacy attached notes as well; derive event advancement and paint from the same values.

theme-self-note-allocation: Both known maker failures independently reproduce, and renamed multiline controls fail too. Legacy drops theme padding from self-arrow preferred width before Step1Abstract-equivalent note placement: cerulean Padding5 loses2*5 unscaled units (10.4167 in scaled SVG). Activation borders and glyph widths agree. Teoz shares that missing preferred width and also has a participant-origin translation and body-envelope discrepancy: known participant x is+5.2083 scaled, canvas width and height each-5.2083. Java composes the real head width, posC2+complete self width, note width and head/body/head envelope before wrapper insets. Rust reconstructs these independently through theme-specific participant padding, self width and raw_body_bottom. The exact required dependency paths are those functions, not a style-border fallback or a generic font waiver. The extra Teoz origin/envelope differences are not proven to have a single scalar cause. Causal next step: Unify the sequenceDiagramPadder-derived self-arrow preferred dimensions at all note/canvas consumers; separately port Teoz participant Real origins and head/body/head wrapper dimensions through the same component measurements. Preserve both failing pairs and require independently checked controls for all affected dimensions. No compensating offsets.

raw-link-second-display: Preserving raw link escapes in the outer Display conversion is correct but insufficient. Java applies Display#getWithNewlines again to the parsed URL label and composes AtomVerticalTexts. Rust push_literal retains path\ntext as one run. Both fresh engines lose one line and its preferred height; the measured and painted note envelope is wrong. This is a shared creole model dependency, not a font difference. Causal next step: Represent multiline hyperlink label atoms and propagate their complete dimensions; preserve the outer raw-boundary semantics.
